        ## Harness issues — found 2026-09-17 reviewing the completed reproducibility lock
        
        Issues 22–27 come from a second review, asked for after issues 12–21 were closed: read the whole
        reproducibility lock again — code, baselines and documentation — against
        [plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md](plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md), and look for
        problems nobody had disclosed yet. The plan itself is fully implemented; `selfcheck`, `env` (24/24)
        and a full `check` (both analyses, real driver runs) all pass on the tree as it stands. These six
        are what the review found on top of that.
        
        **None of them invalidates a recorded number.** Issue 22 is the one worth fixing first: it is a
        hole in the comparator, which is the component whose entire job is to notice. Issue 24 was fixed
        on sight, because leaving it would have made this file contradict itself. The rest are recorded
        and open.
        
        **Only issue 23 predates this work** — the write it describes has been in `FindBHWindow.py` since
        2021. 22, 25 and 26 arrived with `tests/repro.py`; 24 with the audit bookkeeping; 27 is a sentence
        that was true when written and was made stale by the lock's own §6 change.
        
        ### 22. `compare()` treats NaN as a match — **Medium**
        
        **What.** The float comparison is `if diff > atol + rtol * abs(b)`, and every comparison against
        NaN is `False`. A candidate value of NaN therefore passes against any baseline value, for every
        leaf in the tight and pvalue classes: fitted parameters and their errors, `minNll`, `chi2`,
        `chi2/ndof`, postfit bin contents, the data integral, and every p-value. Confirmed directly:
        `compare({'minNll': 1259.11}, {'minNll': nan})` returns `[]`, while the same comparison against
        `inf` correctly fails.
        
        **Where.** [tests/repro.py:101](tests/repro.py#L101), the `diff > atol + rtol * abs(b)` test in
        `compare()`.
        
        **Affects.** Both analyses. The exposure is a fit that fails into NaN rather than failing loudly —
        which is precisely the failure mode this harness is the compensating control for, since XMLReader
        and quickFit only warn and still return 0 (see the first table above). In practice such a fit would
        probably also move `status`/`covQual`, which are exact-compared and would fail, and a NaN in the
        postfit histogram would likely disturb the data integral too — so it is unlikely that a NaN run
        passes `check` outright. But that is luck, not design, and the one component that exists to catch
        this is the one that silently agrees.
        
        **Fix.** Guard the float branch: a mismatch if exactly one of baseline and candidate is NaN, a
        match if both are, and the existing tolerance test otherwise (`math.isnan`). Roughly three lines,
        plus a `selfcheck` case for each of the three combinations. Worth doing even though `status` would
        probably catch it anyway — the check is cheap and the alternative is relying on a coincidence.
        
        ### 23. `check` overwrites `bump.png` and `BH_statistics.png` in the repository root — **Low**
        
        **What.** `FindBHWindow.py` writes its two plots with bare relative filenames, so they land in the
        process's working directory rather than in the run folder. `check` runs each driver from the
        repository root, so a `check` that exercises J50 rewrites those two files at the top of the
        repository — outside `run/check_scratch/`, which is the only place the README and
        `doc/IMPROVEMENTS.md` say `check` writes.
        
        **Where.** [python/FindBHWindow.py:88](python/FindBHWindow.py#L88) and
        [python/FindBHWindow.py:91](python/FindBHWindow.py#L91) (`filename="bump.png"`,
        `filename="BH_statistics.png"`); [tests/repro.py:787](tests/repro.py#L787), where `_run_driver`
        does `cd "{REPO_ROOT}"`.
        
        **Affects.** Anyone who keeps the real J50 BumpHunter plots at the repository root: a later `check`
        replaces them with the scratch run's, with no warning. Nothing tracked changes — `*.png` is
        gitignored, which is why `git status` stayed clean and this went unnoticed through the whole
        implementation. The behaviour predates this work (the write has been there since 2021-11-02, and
        every real J50 driver run does the same thing); what is new is the isolation claim written around
        it in 2026-09-16's documentation.
        
        **Fix.** Either pass a folder-qualified filename from `run_anaFit.py` into `plot_bump`/`plot_stat`
        so the plots land beside the rest of the run's output — which is where they belong anyway, and
        would make them visible to `directory_listing` — or, if that is out of scope for a fit-path change,
        state the behaviour in the README's Reproducibility section and in `doc/IMPROVEMENTS.md` so the
        isolation claim stops being broader than the truth.
        
        ### 24. This file said issues 14–21 were still proposals after they were fixed — **Low** — **Fixed 2026-09-17 12:45**
        
        **Fixed.** The paragraph now states that all ten are fixed and that each `Fix` below is the
        proposal that was carried out. Corrected rather than left open, because a file whose stated purpose
        is honest disclosure cannot carry a false statement about its own contents while new issues are
        appended beneath it.
        
        **What.** The preamble to the 12–21 section read "**Below, issues 12 and 13 are fixed … every other
        `Fix` is still a proposal awaiting review, not a record of work done**". That was accurate when
        written on 2026-09-16, and stopped being accurate on 2026-09-17 as 14 through 21 were fixed in turn
        — each entry's own header was updated to say **Fixed**, but the paragraph introducing them was not.
        
        **Where.** `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, the paragraph opening the "Harness issues — found 2026-09-16"
        section.
        
        **Affects.** A reader trusting the section header over the individual entries would conclude eight
        open harness bugs remained. Nothing in the code.
        
        ### 25. The pyBumpHunter egg check compares against a hardcoded constant — **Low**
        
        **What.** Plan §1's rule is that every expected value is parsed from the file that already declares
        it, "without inventing a new source of truth". The egg check breaks that rule: it compares the
        installed egg's version against `EXPECTED_PYBUMPHUNTER_EGG_VERSION = "0.4.3.dev16+g91f49a6"`, a
        constant in the harness, rather than against the short form of the pyBumpHunter SHA it already
        parses out of `install.sh` (`91f49a622bd…` → `91f49a6`). Related, in the same check:
        `find_pybumphunter_egg_version` takes `sorted(glob(...))[0]`, so if the venv ever holds two eggs it
        reports whichever sorts first rather than noticing the ambiguity.
        
        **Where.** [tests/repro.py:267](tests/repro.py#L267) (the constant),
        [tests/repro.py:311-316](tests/repro.py#L311-L316) (`find_pybumphunter_egg_version`),
        [tests/repro.py:484-486](tests/repro.py#L484-L486) (the check).
        
        **Affects.** Nothing today — the constant agrees with the pin, and `env` passes 24/24. It bites
        whenever the pyBumpHunter pin in `install.sh` is deliberately bumped: the clone SHA check passes,
        the egg check fails, and its message blames the egg for disagreeing with a constant nobody thought
        to update, rather than saying the venv needs rebuilding against the new pin. The check is right
        about *what* is wrong and misleading about *why*.
        
        **Fix.** Derive the expected short SHA from the already-parsed `install_pins["pyBumpHunter"]` and
        assert the egg version ends with `+g<short>`, keeping the `0.4.3.dev16` part out of it (it is
        pyBumpHunter's own versioning, not something this repository pins). Fail with both the installed
        and the expected value, as now. Optionally report a second egg as its own failure instead of
        silently picking one.
        
        ### 26. A leaf whose *type* changes crashes the comparator; a malformed baseline crashes `env` — **Low**
        
        **What.** Two diagnosability gaps, both turning a reportable condition into a traceback. In
        `compare()`, a baseline float against a candidate string reaches `abs(c - b)` and raises
        `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'str' and 'float'` instead of being reported as a
        mismatch (the type guard on the line above tests only the *baseline* value's type). In
        `_report_env()`, a baseline file missing `provenance`, `provenance["versions"]` or
        `provenance["binary_sha256"]` raises `KeyError` rather than saying which file is malformed.
        
        **Where.** [tests/repro.py:94](tests/repro.py#L94) and [tests/repro.py:101](tests/repro.py#L101);
        [tests/repro.py:553](tests/repro.py#L553) and [tests/repro.py:576](tests/repro.py#L576).
        
        **Affects.** Neither can happen while the extractors and `record` are the only writers of these
        documents — the types are fixed by the ROOT calls that produce them, and `record` always writes a
        complete provenance block. Both become reachable the moment a baseline is hand-edited or produced
        by a future variant of the tooling, which is exactly when a clear message matters most.
        
        **Fix.** In `compare()`, test both values' types and report a type change as a mismatch in its own
        right. In `_report_env()`, skip a baseline whose provenance is missing or incomplete with a named
        warning rather than raising. Four or five lines each; `selfcheck` can cover the comparator half
        with no ROOT.
        
        ### 27. `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` still call the sub-frameworks "CERN GitLab" ones — **Low**
        
        **What.** Both open by describing the framework as wrapping "three CERN GitLab C++
        sub-frameworks", while the links beside that phrase point at GitHub and `install.sh` has cloned
        from `github.com/tofitsch/...` since the plan's §6 repoint. The sentence was true when it was
        written on 2026-09-15; §6 made it stale on 2026-09-16 and neither file was revisited. The upstream
        project genuinely is hosted on CERN GitLab (the README's Links section still points there), so the
        phrase is half-true, which is the awkward kind.
        
        **Where.** [README.md:3-4](README.md#L3-L4), [CLAUDE.md:7-8](CLAUDE.md#L7-L8).
        
        **Affects.** Documentation only. The risk is a reader concluding the clone URLs still resolve at
        CERN GitLab, which is the exact confusion §6 existed to remove — the GitLab URLs are unreachable,
        which is why they were repointed.
        
        **Fix.** Say the sub-frameworks are mirrored on GitHub and cloned from there at pinned SHAs, and
        keep the CERN GitLab reference where it is accurate (the upstream project and its documentation).
        Note that `CLAUDE.md` carries unrelated uncommitted changes in the working tree — read it before
        editing, as the plan's §7 already warns.

      content:
        """Prove env's pyBumpHunter egg check now follows install.sh's pin.

        Builds a throwaway root: the four clones symlinked to the real ones, plus a
        copy of install.sh whose pyBumpHunter pin has had its first character changed.
        Nothing tracked is touched - the real tree is only read.
        """
        import pathlib
        import re
        import sys
        import tempfile

        REPO = pathlib.Path("/afs/cern.ch/user/h/hhook/FrequentistFramework")
        sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "tests"))
        import repro  # noqa: E402

        EGG_CHECK = "pyBumpHunter installed egg version"


        def egg_check_in(root):
            checks, _, _ = repro.run_env_checks(root)
            return next((c for c in checks if c[0] == EGG_CHECK), None)


        def build_root(tmp, mutate):
            root = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            for name in repro.FRAMEWORKS:
                (root / name).symlink_to(REPO / name)
            text = (REPO / "install.sh").read_text()
            if mutate:
                pin = re.search(r"cd pyBumpHunter\n\n?git check" + r"out ([0-9a-f]{40})", text).group(1)
                bumped = ("f" if pin[0] != "f" else "e") + pin[1:]
                text = text.replace(pin, bumped)
                print(f"mutated pin: short form {pin[:7]} -> {bumped[:7]}")
            (root / "install.sh").write_text(text)
            return root


        for mutate in (False, True):
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                name, ok, detail = egg_check_in(build_root(tmp, mutate))
                print(f"{'mutated' if mutate else 'unmutated'} pin -> [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {detail}")

        print("\nThe real tree was only read; nothing tracked was modified.")

       178:# Reproducibility
       179-
       180-`tests/repro.py` is a regression harness for the two Run 2 dijet TLA fits (J100 481-3000 GeV,
       181-J50 302-2997 GeV) — the only two analyses this repository currently produces. It cannot prove the
       182-physics is *right*, only that a change did not move it; see
       183-[plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md](plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md) for the
       184-design and [doc/IMPROVEMENTS.md](doc/IMPROVEMENTS.md) for how it works.
       185-
       186-```
       187-python3 tests/repro.py selfcheck            # comparator's own test, no ROOT, instant
       188-python3 tests/repro.py env                  # software pins vs what's actually on disk/CVMFS
       189-python3 tests/repro.py check --quick        # J100 only, ~1-2 min
       190-python3 tests/repro.py check                # both analyses, incl. J50's BumpHunter masking, ~6 min
       191-```
       192-
       193-**`record`/`check` need `python3` itself to already have PyROOT importable** — the plain lxplus
       194-system `python3` has this with no setup at all, which is what the driver subprocesses they launch
       195-are sourced against anyway. Run them from a shell that has *not* activated
       196-`pyBumpHunter/pyBH_env` (it carries no ROOT bindings, only the pyBumpHunter egg) or sourced an
       197-ATLAS/lsetup environment that puts a different `python3` first on `$PATH` — either produces a
       198-clear `ERROR: ... has no ROOT module` rather than running.
       199-
       200-`check` re-runs the driver(s) with `OUT_DIR` pointed at a scratch directory — `run/` itself is
       201-never touched — and compares the fitted parameters, `minNll`, chi2/p-values, postfit bins and
       202-BumpHunter output against `tests/baseline_J100.json`/`baseline_J50.json`. One exception to that
       203-isolation, inherited rather than introduced: the BumpHunter step writes `bump.png` and
       204-`BH_statistics.png` with bare relative filenames, so any run that reaches it — a real J50 fit or a
       205-`check` — rewrites those two files at the repository root
       206-([KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md) issue 23).

       # Improvements

       One living document for the whole reproducibility/refactoring effort: what the framework now
       does, why it was changed, and how it is meant to be used. Rewritten in place as things evolve —
       this describes the *current* state, not history. History is [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md).

       ## Reproducibility harness (`tests/repro.py`)

       **Why.** Before any significant change to the repository, there has to be a way to *prove* a
       change did not move a physics number. Plan:
       [plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md](../plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md).

       **What exists now.** Four subcommands:

       ```
       python3 tests/repro.py selfcheck
       python3 tests/repro.py env
       python3 tests/repro.py record {J100,J50} [DIR] [--force --reason "..."]
       python3 tests/repro.py check [--quick] [--from DIR [--analysis {J100,J50}]] [--tol-scale SCALE]
       ```

       `selfcheck` runs the comparator against synthetic data — no ROOT, no ATLAS environment, instant.

       `env` verifies the software stack against the files that already declare each pin, rather than
       inventing a second source of truth: the four sub-framework SHAs in `install.sh` against
       `git rev-parse HEAD` in each gitignored clone; the RooFitExtensions SHA in each sub-framework's
       own live `scripts/install_roofitext.sh`; agreement of the `lsetup "views …"` line across all
       three `setup_lxplus.sh`; the pyBumpHunter venv's `pyvenv.cfg` against that view and Python 3.9.12;
       the installed egg's version against the short SHA of the pyBumpHunter pin it parsed from
       `install.sh` (so a deliberate pin bump reports "the venv needs rebuilding", not a disagreement with
       a constant — [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md) issue 25, fixed 2026-09-17); and that none of
       the four clones have modified tracked files. It also computes the SHA-256 of the two built binaries and compares them against the
       digests in every existing baseline's provenance — a rebuilt `XMLReader` or `quickFit` 
       [... 10,788 more characters truncated ...]

## Verdict

**The plan is fully implemented.** I checked every requirement in §1–§7 and Verification steps 1–7 against the tree, and re-ran the harness rather than trusting the write-ups:

- `selfcheck` → 3 PASS blocks, exit 0
- `env` → **24/24 PASS**, versions match both baselines' provenance, exit 0
- `check --from run/run_481_3000_sixPar` → env + input hashes + J100 comparison, **PASS**, exit 0 (this path had never been exercised in any changelog entry — it works)
- Baseline contents match the plan's Verification step 4 numbers exactly: `minNll` 1259.1119375388664, `p6` 0.0478363, J50 rebinned `pval` 0.0024417, BH window 582–662, `global_Pval` 0.0322
- §6 is real on disk: `.gitmodules` and `scripts/install_roofitext.sh` are gone, [install.sh](install.sh) clones from GitHub with the four SHAs unchanged
- Working tree clean, baselines and both new docs tracked

Two deviations from the plan's literal text exist and are both deliberate and documented (`--rtol`→`--tol-scale`, issue 19; the "note" tolerance class replaced by excluding `provenance` from the comparison, issue 16). I found no requirement silently dropped.

## Four new findings, none disclosed anywhere

All four are the same class issue 26 named — *a reportable condition turned into a traceback* — and that fix only hardened two of the places where it occurs. None can move or invalidate a recorded number.

**1. A missing input spectrum crashes `check` instead of failing it** — Medium. [tests/repro.py:872-874](tests/repro.py#L872-L874): `sha256_of()` on a path from the baseline's `input_sha256` with no existence guard. Confirmed by running it: `FileNotFoundError: .../Input/data/dijetTLA/moved_away.root`, no message about what it means. Plan §2 promises `check` "verifies them before running anything and stops on a mismatch" — a moved or deleted input is exactly that, and during the refactor the harness exists for, `Input/` being reorganised is a likely event. [tests/repro.py:829](tests/repro.py#L829) has the same hole in `record`'s provenance block.

**2. A PostFit directory without the expected histograms crashes the extractor** — Low/Medium. [tests/repro.py:734-741](tests/repro.py#L734-L741): `d.Get("chi2")` returning a null pointer reaches `h.GetNbinsX()`. Confirmed on a synthetic file: `AttributeError: 'TObject' object has no attribute 'GetNbinsX'`. Same for `postfit`/`data` in a `*_rebinned` dir, and for `f.Get("fitResult")` at [tests/repro.py:706-707](tests/repro.py#L706-L707). The comment above `extract_postfit` says `compare()` catches a missing or renamed directory as a missing key — true for a renamed directory, false for one whose *contents* changed, which is what a rewrite of `ExtractPostfitFromWS.py` would produce.

**3. `_view_binary_version` catches neither a timeout nor an OSError** — Low. [tests/repro.py:395](tests/repro.py#L395): `subprocess.run(..., timeout=30)` with no `try`. `_atlas_probe` right above it guards both and returns "unavailable" precisely because §1 says to record rather than assert these. A stalled CVMFS mount — not exotic on lxplus — takes `env`, `record` and `check` down with a traceback instead of recording `cmake: unavailable`.

**4. `record`'s cross-baseline versions read was left unhardened** — Low. [tests/repro.py:817](tests/repro.py#L817): `json.loads(...)["provenance"]["versions"]` raises `KeyError` on a malformed sibling baseline, which is the identical expression `_report_env` was hardened against under issue 26.

## What I did not find

Below is each finding in full, then what ties them to issue 26.

---

## 1. A missing input spectrum crashes `check` — Medium

**The code.** [tests/repro.py:862-880](tests/repro.py#L862-L880):

```python
mismatches = [f"  {rel}: baseline={expected} now={sha256_of(REPO_ROOT / rel)}"
              for rel, expected in sorted(baseline["provenance"]["input_sha256"].items())
              if sha256_of(REPO_ROOT / rel) != expected]
```

`sha256_of()` is [`hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes())`](tests/repro.py#L355) with no existence guard, so a path recorded in the baseline that no longer exists raises out of the comprehension. Confirmed by running it against a baseline naming a moved file:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../Input/data/dijetTLA/moved_away.root'
```

**Why it matters more than it looks.** Plan §2 makes this function the gate: "`check` verifies them before running anything and stops on a mismatch." A deleted or moved input *is* the condition §2 exists to catch — arguably the most serious form of it, since a renamed input means the baselines have stopped describing anything at all. It is the one input state that produces no diagnosis.

The trigger is not hypothetical. The harness's stated job is to run repeatedly *while* the repository is rewritten, and `Input/` holds 313 spectra across five analysis flavours that the plan itself calls dead weight. A refactor that tidies `Input/` is a likely early move, and the first `check` afterwards reports a stack trace rather than "input spectrum changed for J100".

**Same hole in `record`.** [tests/repro.py:829](tests/repro.py#L829) builds `input_sha256` with the same unguarded call, from `spec["inputs"]` — so a driver whose input path has moved crashes `record` too, after the env probes have already run.

**One adjacent observation, not a bug.** `check` iterates the *baseline's* recorded inputs while `record` iterates `ANALYSES[...]["inputs"]`. That asymmetry is right — it is what keeps `check` path-independent — but it means a driver that gains a fifth input is unguarded until the baseline is re-cut. Worth knowing during the refactor. (`spec` is dead in that function as a result.)

---

## 2. A PostFit/FitResult file whose *contents* changed crashes the extractor — Low/Medium

**The code.** [tests/repro.py:734-735](tests/repro.py#L734-L735):

```python
d = f.Get(name)
h = d.Get("chi2")
chi2[name] = {h.GetXaxis().GetBinLabel(i): h.GetBinContent(i) for i in range(1, h.GetNbinsX() + 1)}
```

`d.Get("chi2")` on a directory without that histogram returns a null pointer, which PyROOT hands back as a bare `TObject`. Confirmed on a synthetic file:

```
AttributeError: 'TObject' object has no attribute 'GetNbinsX'
```

The same pattern sits at [tests/repro.py:737](tests/repro.py#L737) (`postfit`/`data` in a `*_rebinned` directory), at [tests/repro.py:706-707](tests/repro.py#L706-L707) (`f.Get("fitResult")` → `fr.floatParsFinal()`), and at [tests/repro.py:748](tests/repro.py#L748) (`extract_bhresults` doing `bh["pyBHresult"]` → `KeyError` on a truncated or restructured `BHresults.json`). `ROOT.TFile.Open` on a corrupt or truncated file also returns a nullptr, so `f.Get` fails the same way one line later — and `f.Close()` is skipped on every one of these paths.

**The precise shape of the gap: presence is guarded, content is not.** [`extract_variant`](tests/repro.py#L754-L767) checks `fit_path.is_file()` and `post_path.is_file()` and returns `None` for a missing file, which `check` turns into a clean `FAIL: ... has no FitResult/PostFit`. So "the file isn't there" is handled well. "The file is there and is not what we expect" is the unhandled case.

**Why this one is pointed at the refactor specifically.** The comment above `extract_postfit` says the directory names need not be known in advance because `compare()` catches a renamed directory as a missing key — true, and a good design. But the *histogram* names inside (`chi2`, `postfit`, `data`) are hardcoded, and that half of the contract has no such protection. [python/ExtractPostfitFromWS.py](python/ExtractPostfitFromWS.py) is squarely in the set of files the plan expects to be rewritten. A rewrite that renames the chi2 histogram, or creates a directory before filling it, should print `missing: unmasked.chi2.J100yStar06_rebinned.pval` — the finding the harness exists to produce — and instead prints an `AttributeError` about a `TObject`.

---

## 3. `_view_binary_version` catches nothing — Low

**The code.** [tests/repro.py:384-398](tests/repro.py#L384-L398):

```python
exe = _lcg_view_dir(view) / "bin" / binary
if not exe.is_file():
    return f"unavailable (no {exe})"
proc = subprocess.run([str(exe), *version_args], text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=30)
if proc.returncode != 0:
    return f"unavailable (exit {proc.returncode}: ...)"
return proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[0]
```

Three unguarded exits, all on the happy path:

1. **`subprocess.TimeoutExpired`** after 30 s. Both binaries live on `/cvmfs/sft.cern.ch`; a cold cache or a stalled mount is routine on lxplus, not exotic.
2. **`OSError`** — including the TOCTOU window between `is_file()` and `run()`, which on CVMFS is exactly when a mount is most likely to go away.
3. **`IndexError`** — `"".strip().splitlines()` is `[]`, so a binary that exits 0 while printing its version to stderr takes `[0]` off an empty list.

**The irony, and the contract it breaks.** Its sibling [`_atlas_probe`](tests/repro.py#L359-L377) wraps the identical call in `try/except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError)` and documents why: *"Never raises — plan section 1 records these values rather than asserting them, precisely because they cannot be pinned from this repository."* `_view_binary_version` serves that same §1 clause — the cmake and ROOT versions are the canonical "record, never assert" values — and a crash is the hardest possible assert. The plan's amended §1 is emphatic that version drift must never fail the command, because "a check that fails for reasons nobody can act on is a check that gets ignored". A slow CVMFS mount is precisely a reason nobody can act on.

**Blast radius.** `run_env_checks()` calls both `resolve_cmake_version` and `resolve_root_version`, so this takes down `env`, `record` and `check` alike, before any fit runs. The recorded value should read `unavailable (timed out after 30s)` — which, per §1's closing line, is itself a true and useful thing for a baseline to say.

---

## 4. `record`'s cross-baseline read was left unhardened — Low

**The code.** [tests/repro.py:814-823](tests/repro.py#L814-L823):

```python
other = "J50" if args.analysis == "J100" else "J100"
other_path = REPO_ROOT / "tests" / f"baseline_{other}.json"
if other_path.exists():
    other_versions = json.loads(other_path.read_text())["provenance"]["versions"]
```

`json.loads` raises `ValueError` on invalid JSON; the two subscripts raise `KeyError` on a missing or partial provenance block.

**Why it stands out.** This implements plan §1's "record warns when it is about to write a versions block that disagrees with the other baseline's" — and [`_report_env`](tests/repro.py#L598-L615) reads *the same field of the same file for the same purpose* and was hardened under issue 26, printing `WARNING: <file> has no usable provenance block (missing ...) - skipping its comparisons`. So one subcommand degrades gracefully on a malformed baseline and the other dies. Issue 26's fix simply did not carry across.

Also brittle, though within spec: `other` is a binary J100/J50 flip. Plan §1 says "Both baselines carry the same versions block", written for exactly two analyses, so this is correct today — but a third entry in `ANALYSES` would silently compare against J100 only.

---

## In one sentence

In four places the harness hits a problem it should *report* and instead crashes.

## What that means

`tests/repro.py` is supposed to end in one of two ways: **PASS**, or **FAIL** with a line saying what moved. A crash is a third ending nobody planned for — you get a Python stack trace, no explanation, and no idea whether the fit changed or the tool is broken.

The four places:

| If this happens… | You should see | You actually get |
|---|---|---|
| An input spectrum has been moved or deleted | `FAIL: input spectrum changed for J100` | `FileNotFoundError` |
| A PostFit file is missing a histogram inside it | `missing: unmasked.chi2....pval` | `AttributeError: 'TObject' has no attribute...` |
| CVMFS is slow and `cmake --version` times out | `cmake: unavailable (timed out)` — just a note, not a failure | crash, and `env`/`record`/`check` all die with it |
| A baseline file is half-written | `WARNING: ... skipping its comparisons` | `KeyError` |

## Two things worth knowing

**Nothing is at risk.** All four crash *instead of* passing, never instead of failing. No recorded number is wrong, no baseline needs re-cutting.

**The danger is behavioural.** You're about to run this thing after every edit while you refactor. The first time it dies on a stack trace because you tidied `Input/`, the natural conclusion is "the harness is broken" — and a harness people stop trusting is a harness people stop running. That is the exact failure the plan spends several paragraphs trying to avoid.

## The link to issue 26

Issue 26 was this same problem, found in two other places, and fixed there. It was fixed even though its trigger was unlikely (someone hand-editing a baseline). These four have likelier triggers — a slow CVMFS mount, or the refactor itself moving files around — and were simply missed when 26 was fixed.

Each fix is a few lines in one file. Happy to do them as one section whenever you want.

Fair challenge, and the honest answer cuts against my own findings.

## Direct answer: 2 of the 4, and arguably 3

| # | Reachable by a careful user? | |
|---|---|---|
| 4. Malformed baseline crashes `record` | **No** | Only fires if someone hand-edits a baseline. The docs say re-cut with `record --force --reason`. Follow that and it can never happen. |
| 1. Missing input crashes `check` | **Barely** | Four tracked files that nobody moves by accident. Only reachable if *you* deliberately reorganise `Input/` — and then you already know why it broke. |
| 3. CVMFS timeout | **No, but rare** | Not user error, pure infrastructure. And when CVMFS stalls, the drivers won't run either — you have a broken session, not a confusing harness. |
| 2. PostFit contents changed | **Yes, during the refactor** | The only one triggered by the work you're about to do rather than by a mistake. |

## And the complaint was overstated

I said a traceback gives you "no explanation". Re-reading them, that's not really true:

- `FileNotFoundError: .../Input/data/dijetTLA/moved_away.root` — names the exact file
- `KeyError: 'provenance'` — names the exact missing field
- `AttributeError: 'TObject' has no attribute 'GetNbinsX'` in `extract_postfit` — points at the line doing `d.Get("chi2")`

The gap between that and a clean `FAIL:` line is polish, not information. I framed it as a legibility cliff; it's a legibility bump.

## So: don't fix them

Record all four in KNOWN_ISSUES as disclosed-and-left-alone. That is what the file is for, and the plan says so in as many words: *"Recording is the obligation; fixing is a choice… a framework this size would drown in defensive code written for situations that never arise."* Three of these four are situations that never arise.

If you want exactly one, take **#2** — four null-checks in the extractors, because it's the only one the refactor itself will trip, and it's the difference between `missing: unmasked.chi2.J100yStar06_rebinned.pval` and a traceback at the moment you're deciding whether your rewrite changed the physics. Even that is defensible to defer.

One consistency note worth having on record: this same reasoning applies backwards to **issue 26**, which was fixed on a weaker trigger than any of these (a hand-edited baseline). The bar was set too low then. The right response is to leave the bar where you actually want it now, not to chase parity with a past decision.

Want me to write the four up as recorded-not-fixed entries (28–31) with that reasoning stated, and leave the code alone?

       # CLAUDE.md

       This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

       ## What this is

       ATLAS statistical-fit framework for dijet/TLA bump-hunt analyses. It wraps three C++
       sub-frameworks cloned at pinned SHAs from their public GitHub mirrors (`xmlAnaWSBuilder`,
       `quickFit`, `workspaceCombiner`) plus `pyBumpHunter`
       behind Python drivers that template XML workspace cards, run the fit, and extract postfit
       histograms, fit parameters and p-values.

       ## Commands

       All commands must be run **from the repository root** — `setup.sh` and
       `scripts/setup_buildAndFit.sh` abort if `xmlAnaWSBuilder/` and `quickFit/` are not in `$PWD`.

       ```bash
       setupATLAS && lsetup git    # lxplus/CVMFS environment first
       . install.sh                # clone + cmake-build the sub-frameworks (one-off, ~long)
       . setup.sh                  # source (do NOT execute) before any run — sets $_DIRFIT etc.
       . scripts/run_anaFit.sh     # main entry point
       ```

       `install.sh` and `setup.sh` must be **sourced**; they `cd` around and export env vars.

       Output defaults to `<repo>/run/` (`out_dir=${OUT_DIR:-$PWD/run}` at the top of each driver) —
       every output lands under `$out_dir/run_<rangelow>_<rangehigh>_<n>Par/`. Set `OUT_DIR` to an
       EOS path for HTCondor toy studies; AFS home quotas are too small for hundreds of runs.

       Other drivers: `scripts/run_nloFit.sh` (NLO-template fit, uses `setup_buildCombineFit.sh`),
       `scripts/run_anaFit_syst.sh`, `scripts/run_anaFitLoop.sh`, `scripts/run_swiftFit.py`.

       There is no linter config or CI on this branch. `tests/repro.py` is a reproducibility-lock
       harness scoped to the J50/J100 fits only (`env`/`record`/`check`/`selfcheck` subcommands, see
       the README's Reproducibility section) — it is not a general test suite for the repository.

       ## Architecture

       The fit is a template-substitution pipeline, not a library. [python/run_anaFit.py](python/run_anaFit.py)
       is the orchestrator;

       +## Triaging issues

       +Everything that *fails closed* — crashes, tracebacks, a check that stops instead of passing — is
       +a lower tier however ugly it looks. It cannot put a wrong number in front of anyone. Fix those
       +when they are cheap or when they sit on a path about to be rewritten; otherwise record them and
       +move on. Defensive code written for situations that never arise is its own cost.

Added to [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) as a new **Triaging issues** section, just above Planning.

## Would any of the four have allowed it? No — none of them.

All four crash. A crash cannot produce a result at all, let alone a wrong one. They are the *opposite* of the class you're describing:

| | Your priority class | These four |
|---|---|---|
| Analysis completes | yes | no |
| You get a number | yes, and it's wrong | no |
| You notice | no | immediately |

This is the sharpest possible version of the point I conceded last turn: I ranked them by how ugly the failure looks, and you're ranking them by whether a wrong number survives. On your ranking all four are bottom tier, and that's the correct ranking.

## What *has* been in that class here

Worth knowing the shape of the real thing, since three examples already exist in this repository:

- **XMLReader/quickFit warn and return 0** — a failed fit looks successful. Still open, deliberately; `tests/repro.py check` exists as the compensating control.
- **Issue 22, NaN treated as a match** — a fit that failed into NaN could pass `check` clean. This one was genuinely in your top class, and it's already fixed (2026-09-17).
- **`re.sub("PAR1", …)` before `PAR10`** — would corrupt a ten-parameter card silently. Harmless at six parameters, so recorded and left alone.

Notice the pattern: every one of them is something that *keeps going*. That is the tell.

So the four new findings should be recorded, not fixed — and now there's a written rule in CLAUDE.md that says why, so the next review doesn't rediscover them and rank them high again. Want me to write them up as entries 28–31 under that framing?

       # Known issues

       Known bugs, limitations and deliberately unguarded edge cases, stated openly. Recording an
       issue here is the obligation; fixing it is a choice — not every problem needs to be fixed, and
       not every edge case needs to be explicitly guarded, or a framework this size would drown in
       defensive code written for situations that never arise. What is not acceptable is a known
       problem that is *undisclosed*: the next person then rediscovers it as a wrong physics number
       rather than as a documented limitation.

       Each entry: what it is, where it lives, what it affects, and whether it is deliberately left
       alone. Updated whenever an issue is found, fixed, or consciously accepted.

       # Improvements

       One living document for the whole reproducibility/refactoring effort: what the framework now
       does, why it was changed, and how it is meant to be used. Rewritten in place as things evolve —
       this describes the *current* state, not history. History is [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md).

       ## Reproducibility harness (`tests/repro.py`)

       **Why.** Before any significant change to the repository, there has to be a way to *prove* a
       change did not move a physics number. Plan:
       [plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md](../plans/2026-09-15-reproducibility-lock.md).

       **What exists now.** Four subcommands:

       ```
       python3 tests/repro.py selfcheck
       python3 tests/repro.py env
       python3 tests/repro.py record {J100,J50} [DIR] [--force --reason "..."]
       python3 tests/repro.py check [--quick] [--from DIR [--analysis {J100,J50}]] [--tol-scale SCALE]
       ```

       `selfcheck` runs the comparator against synthetic data — no ROOT, no ATLAS environment, instant.

       `env` verifies the software stack against the files that already declare each pin, rather than
       inventing a second source of truth: the four sub-framework SHAs in `install.sh` against
       `git rev-parse HEAD` in each gitignored clone; the RooFitExtensions SHA in each sub-framework's
       own live `scripts/install_roofitext.sh`; agreement of the `lsetup "views …"` line across all
       three `setup_lxplus.sh`; the pyBumpHunter venv's `pyvenv.cfg` against that view and Python 3.9.12;
       the installed egg's version against the short SHA of the pyBumpHunter pin it parsed from
       `install.sh` (so a deliberate pin bump reports "the venv needs rebuilding", not a disagreement with
       a constant — [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md) issue 25, fixed 2026-09-17); and that none of
       the four clones have modified tracked files. It also computes the SHA-256 of the two built binaries and compares them against the
       digests in every existing baseline's provenance — a rebuilt `XMLReader` or `quickFit`

       193-**`record`/`check` need `python3` itself to already have PyROOT importable** — the plain lxplus
       194-system `python3` has this with no setup at all, which is what the driver subprocesses they launch
       195-are sourced against anyway. Run them from a shell that has *not* activated
       196-`pyBumpHunter/pyBH_env` (it carries no ROOT bindings, only the pyBumpHunter egg) or sourced an
       197-ATLAS/lsetup environment that puts a different `python3` first on `$PATH` — either produces a
       198-clear `ERROR: ... has no ROOT module` rather than running.
       199-
       200-`check` re-runs the driver(s) with `OUT_DIR` pointed at a scratch directory — `run/` itself is
       201-never touched — and compares the fitted parameters, `minNll`, chi2/p-values, postfit bins and
       202-BumpHunter output against `tests/baseline_J100.json`/`baseline_J50.json`. One exception to that
       203-isolation, inherited rather than introduced: the BumpHunter step writes `bump.png` and
       204-`BH_statistics.png` with bare relative filenames, so any run that reaches it — a real J50 fit or a
       205-`check` — rewrites those two files at the repository root
       206-([KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md) issue 23).

I re-ran the harness and read the plan, `tests/repro.py`, both baselines, and all three documentation surfaces against each other.

**Plan coverage: nothing is missing.** §1–§7 and Verification steps 1–7 are all in place. `selfcheck` passes all three blocks, `env` passes 24/24, and `check --from` against both recorded run directories still PASSes — the committed baselines describe the runs on disk. `.gitmodules` and `scripts/install_roofitext.sh` are gone, `install.sh` clones from GitHub at the unchanged SHAs, and the README/CLAUDE.md corrections §6 asked for are done.

Five problems nobody has disclosed yet. None of them can put a wrong number in front of anyone — under the triage rule in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) the worst two are diagnosis failures, not silent-wrong-result failures.

**1. `record`'s env gate is disabled by the very flag every re-cut needs — Medium.** Issue 14 added "refuse to write when any `env` check fails, unless `--force --reason`". But re-cutting an existing baseline *always* needs `--force` ([tests/repro.py:778](tests/repro.py#L778)), so on the only documented re-cut route the gate is bypassed — and worse, [tests/repro.py:787-793](tests/repro.py#L787-L793) prints the failing checks *only in the branch that refuses*, so a forced re-cut on a tree with a drifted clone says nothing at all. Separately, `cmd_record` calls `run_env_checks()` directly rather than the digest-aware `_report_env()`, so `record`'s gate never includes the binary-SHA comparison that `env` and `check` apply. The gate fires only on a first cut, on pins only.

**2. `provenance.pins` is written and never read back — Medium.** Of the three provenance blocks, `versions` and `binary_sha256` are both compared against the live tree by `_report_env()`; `pins` (plus `active_view`, `pyBH_python_version`, `pyBumpHunter_egg_version`) is recorded at [tests/repro.py:827](tests/repro.py#L827) and never read by anything. Same "computes/records but never compares" defect as issue 12, which was ranked High. Sharpest instance: bump the pyBumpHunter pin in `install.sh`, re-clone, rebuild the venv — the clone-SHA check passes and the egg check passes too, because issue 25's fix derives its expectation from `install.sh` so it moves with the bump. No binary of pyBumpHunter's is hashed. `env` reports 24/24 green while both baselines still record the old SHA, and pyBumpHunter is what computes J50's `global_Pval`. `check` would fail on the moved number, but with `env` green the operator is pushed to the wrong end of the diagnosis order the plan's §5 and the README both establish.

**3. Issue 18 is half fixed and recorded as "Fixed" — Low.** Its own Objective names two defects: hashes checked inside the loop, *and* "`--quick` never looked at J50's inputs at all". The fix addressed the first; `--quick` still checks 2 of the 4, against plan §5's "the four input hashes". Defensible — `--quick` only compares J100's baseline — but nothing says the second half was left deliberately, and the entry and changelog title both read as complete. This repo already has issue 24 for exactly this failure mode.

**4. `parse_install_sh_pins` doesn't reset the pending directory on `cd ..` — Low.** Confirmed: `cd quickFit` / `cd ..` / `git checkout <sha>` attributes the SHA to `quickFit`. Unreachable in `install.sh` as written, and fails loud if it ever were (a mispaired SHA surfaces as a mismatch). Worth noting that the selfcheck comment at [tests/repro.py:245-247](tests/repro.py#L245-L247) claims that arrangement "is the only way to exercise that guard at all" — true of the `!= ".."` guard, but it conceals that the missing reset has no test.

**5. `classify()` silently defaults to bit-exact — Low.** Confirmed: an unclassified float leaf 1e-15 from its baseline fails with `exact match required`. Fails closed, which is the right direction, but the refactor is expected to add quantities and the message won't tell whoever hits it that the leaf just isn't in `TOLERANCE_BY_LEAF`. Related, same line of reasoning: `_check_one` compares a whitelist of three top-level keys ([tests/repro.py:913-916](tests/repro.py#L913-L916)), so a future baseline section would be ignored rather than compared — the plan's "a missing or extra key is a failure in its own right" doesn't hold at the top level. Neither default is stated in the plan or the docs.

[34] ASSISTANT   2026-09-17 11:40:36 UTC   claude-opus-5   [log line 195]

Sorting the five by that criterion changes the order I gave you, and cuts against my own severity labels — worth saying plainly.

## Can cause a false PASS

**Finding 1 (`record --force` bypasses and silences the env gate)** — the only one reachable through normal documented use. The route: a forced re-cut on a tree where a sub-framework clone has hand-modified sources, or a drifted SHA. `env`'s "no modified tracked files" check catches exactly that, and on a *first* cut the gate stops the write. On a re-cut — which always needs `--force`, because the baseline file exists — the gate is skipped and the failing checks are never printed, because [tests/repro.py:787-793](tests/repro.py#L787-L793) prints them only in the branch that refuses. The baseline then encodes numbers produced by an unpinned stack while its provenance records the pinned SHA, and every later `check` on that tree PASSes. The harness's green light stops meaning what the README says it means, and nothing anywhere says so.

A second, narrower form of the same finding: `record` extracts from an existing run directory (default: the *old* run), but records the binaries' digests as they are *now*. A re-cut after a legitimate rebuild therefore pairs old numbers with a new digest — provenance that asserts a binary produced numbers it never produced.

**Finding 5, second half (the top-level whitelist)** — `_check_one` builds `expected` from three named keys ([tests/repro.py:913-916](tests/repro.py#L913-L916)), so if someone extends `record` with a new top-level section and forgets to extend that list, the section is recorded and never compared, and `check` PASSes over it. Needs a harness change to become reachable, but it's silent when it does, and the plan's "a missing or extra key is a failure in its own right" is what would otherwise have covered it.

## Can cause a false FAIL

**Finding 5, first half (`classify()` defaults to bit-exact)** — the most likely of the five to actually bite, and the refactor reaches it without anyone making a mistake. A new leaf name in a baseline (a chi2 histogram gaining a labelled bin, say — `ExtractPostfitFromWS.py` is in the rewrite set) is compared exactly, so it fails on last-ULP drift from a rebuild or another machine while every classified sibling passes within tolerance. Two-step to reach: the new quantity has to be in a re-cut baseline first, since a candidate-only leaf already fails as `unexpected` regardless of class. The confusing part is the shape of the failure — one quantity moving alone reads like a real physics finding.

**Finding 1, in the other direction** — a baseline cut on a drifted tree fails against a later, correct tree, and reports it as "the refactor moved the physics."

**Finding 4 (`cd ..` doesn't reset the pending directory)** — a mispaired pin fails `env` on a correct tree. Not reachable with `install.sh` as it reads today.

## Neither

**Finding 2 (`provenance.pins` never compared)** — I ranked this Medium, and on this criterion that was the wrong frame: it cannot change `check`'s verdict. A stack change that moves a number still fails; one that moves nothing still passes. What it breaks is attribution — `env` passing no longer means "this is the stack the baselines were cut with", only "this tree agrees with `install.sh` as it currently reads", so a genuine failure gets read at the wrong end of the plan's diagnosis order. Costly to diagnose, not capable of misleading anyone about the result.

**Finding 3 (`--quick` checks two of four input hashes)** — no verdict impact in either direction. `--quick` compares only J100's baseline and does check J100's two inputs; J50's are irrelevant to that comparison. It is a stale claim in the issue record, nothing more.

So on the rule in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) — could this let an analysis complete and produce a number that is now wrong — finding 1 is first and finding 5's whitelist half is second. Findings 2, 3 and 4 all fail loud or fail harmlessly.

All six filed as issues 32–37 and all six fixed — every one lived in `tests/repro.py` or its docs, so none hit the "pre-existing bugs are recorded, not fixed" rule that keeps issue 23 open.

**Fixes, in verdict-risk order:**

- **32** (false pass) — the failing `env` checks now print whenever any fail; only the *refusal* stays conditional on `--force`. Since re-cutting always needs `--force`, the report was previously invisible on the only route the README documents.
- **33** (false pass) — `expected` is built by dropping `BASELINE_ONLY_KEYS` instead of naming three keys to keep, so a section added to `record` later is compared by default rather than ignored.
- **34** (false fail) — an unclassified *numeric* leaf now fails with `compared exactly: leaf 'x' has no tolerance class …`. The bit-exact default is unchanged; it fails in the safe direction.
- **35** — `compare_recorded_pins()` compares live pins against each baseline's `provenance.pins` and fails on any difference. It reuses `compare()` rather than adding a second engine: every leaf there is a SHA or version string, which `classify()` already treats as exact. All three provenance blocks are now read back.
- **36** — a `cd` targeting `..`/`../..` voids the pending pairing instead of leaving it set.
- **37** — documentation only: `check` verifies every *selected* analysis's inputs, and `--quick` covers J100's two.

**Verified:** `selfcheck` passes with new cases for all three changed behaviours; `env` is 26/26 (24 plus one pin check per baseline); the new pin check was shown to fail — a throwaway baseline with one bogus SHA produced `FAIL: 1/29`, that check alone, exit 1, then deleted with `git status` clean; `record`'s two refusal paths still refuse and write nothing; and **`check --from` passes unchanged against both recorded run directories**, which is what says the comparison semantics didn't move. No baseline re-cut, no fit re-run, `run/` untouched.

Two things I recorded under issue 32 rather than fixing, because both need a design decision rather than a few lines: `record`'s gate reads the pin checks only, not the binary digests (wiring them in would gate a first cut on the *other* analysis's digests — defensible, but a new check); and `record` can pair an older run directory's numbers with today's provenance. The honest mitigation for the second is "re-run the fit before re-cutting", now in the README.

Written up in [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md) (with the false-pass/false-fail table), [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), [doc/IMPROVEMENTS.md](doc/IMPROVEMENTS.md), [README.md](README.md) and [plans/README.md](plans/README.md). Nothing committed — the issue records and the fixes are separable commits if you'd rather split them.

        getChi2 only counts a bin when `valueErrorData > 0 and postFitValue > 0`.

            for key in f.GetListOfKeys():

                d = f.Get(name)

                    continue

                total = data.GetNbinsX()

        """run_anaFit.py's nPars derivation, lifted verbatim, run against the

        def nPars_as_written(backgroundfile):
            nPars = 5
            if "three" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 3
            if "four" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 4
            elif "five" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 5
            elif "six" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 6
            elif "seven" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 7
            elif "eight" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 8
            elif "nine" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 9
            elif "ten" in backgroundfile:
                nPars = 10
            return nPars


        def pars_in_card(path):
            """The PAR indices the card actually declares - the same regex
            run_anaFit.py already applies to it two lines further down."""
            found = set()
            with open(path) as f:
                for line in f:
                    if "<!--" not in line and "<ModelItem" in line:
                        found.update(int(m) for m in re.findall(r"\[PAR(\d+),", line))
            return sorted(found)


        print(f"{'card':<62} {'nPars':>5} {'PARs in card':>16}")
        for path in sorted(glob.glob("config/*/background_*.template")):
            card = pars_in_card(path)
            n = nPars_as_written(path)
            flag = "" if card and max(card) == n else "   <-- DISAGREES"
            print(f"{path:<62} {n:>5} {str(card):>16}{flag}")

        print("\nSame logic, same card, different directory it happens to sit in:")

    [tool] Bash
      description: Append issues 38-42 to KNOWN_ISSUES
      $ cat >> KNOWN_ISSUES.md <<'EOF'
        
        ## Analysis-path issues — found 2026-09-17 in a fifth review
        
        Issues 38–42 come from a fifth review with a narrower brief than the earlier ones: **what could let
        a mistaken, non-physical analysis pass?** The first four reviews worked over `tests/repro.py`; this
        one worked over the fit path itself — the drivers, `python/run_anaFit.py`,
        `python/ExtractPostfitFromWS.py` and the cards.
        
        **All five are pre-existing, and none is introduced by the reproducibility lock.** Under the
        repository owner's standing instruction — pre-existing fit-path bugs are recorded, not fixed, which
        is what keeps issue 23 open — they are **recorded and left alone** pending a decision. Issue 38 is
        the one worth deciding first: it is a two-word fix and the most direct route to a rejected fit
        looking like an accepted one.
        
        **What protects the two locked analyses, and what does not.** For J50 and J100, `tests/repro.py
        check` compares the recorded outputs, so any of these biting would move a number and fail. Every
        one of them is unguarded for *new* work — a different range, a different parameter count, the
        fits the coming refactor will add — because a new configuration has no baseline. That is where the
        exposure is.
        
        ### 38. `main()` discards `run_anaFit`'s return value, so a rejected fit exits 0 — **High** — **open; recorded, not fixed**
        
        **What.** `run_anaFit()` computes the framework's only "this result is not acceptable" verdict: if
        p(chi2) fails the mask threshold, BumpHunter finds the most significant window, the fit is repeated
        with that window blinded, and if p(chi2) *still* fails, it prints `Exiting with failed fit status.`
        and returns `-1` ([python/run_anaFit.py:431](python/run_anaFit.py#L431)). That verdict is then
        thrown away twice:
        
        1. `main()` calls `run_anaFit(datafile=…)` as a bare statement with no `return`
           ([python/run_anaFit.py:502](python/run_anaFit.py#L502)), so `main()` returns `None` and
           `sys.exit(None)` exits **0**. Confirmed by running the same call shape.
        2. The driver does not check the exit code in any case, and goes straight on to
           `plotPostFit.py` and `plot_postfit.cpp` — so a rejected fit renders `postFit.pdf`,
           `post_fit.pdf` and the EDM plot exactly as an accepted one does
           ([scripts/run_anaFit_run2.sh:77-100](scripts/run_anaFit_run2.sh#L77-L100), and the J50 driver
           likewise).
        
        **Where.** [python/run_anaFit.py:502](python/run_anaFit.py#L502) and
        [python/run_anaFit.py:529](python/run_anaFit.py#L529);
        [scripts/run_anaFit_run2.sh:77](scripts/run_anaFit_run2.sh#L77).
        
        **Affects.** Every analysis, and it is a **false pass** in the strictest sense: the code does the
        work of deciding the fit is unusable, says so on stdout, and then reports success. Nothing in the
        output distinguishes a twice-rejected fit from an accepted one except a line in the log. This is
        the same failure mode as the recorded "XMLReader and quickFit only warn and still return 0", but
        worse, because here the verdict is the framework's *own* and is deliberately computed.
        
        **Fix.** `return run_anaFit(…)` at line 502 — two words, and it changes nothing about any run that
        passes. Then decide separately whether the drivers should stop on it; note that making the exit code
        meaningful may start surfacing real failures in anything that does check it (e.g. the HTCondor
        path), which is the point but is a behaviour change worth making deliberately.
        
        ### 39. The p(chi2) gate reads a different histogram depending on whether a mask is active — **Medium** — **open; recorded, not fixed**
        
        **What.** `build_fit_extract` returns the p-value the threshold decision is made on, and picks its
        source by whether a mask range was passed:
        
        ```python
        if maskmin > -1 or maskmax > -1:
            pval = pfe.GetPval(channel+"_bkgonly_rebinned")  # should be <channel> or <channel>_rebinned?
        else:
            pval = pfe.GetPval(channel+"_rebinned")          # should be <channel> or <channel>_rebinned?
        ```
        
        So the *initial* gate reads `<channel>_rebinned` and the *masked* accept/reject decision reads
        `<channel>_bkgonly_rebinned`. The two are different numbers, and the comment — in the code as
        written — shows the choice was never settled.
        
        **Where.** [python/run_anaFit.py:127-131](python/run_anaFit.py#L127-L131).
        
        **Affects.** Both gates, in principle. From the recorded baselines the two differ by roughly 1–2%
        relative:
        
        | Fit | `_rebinned` | `_bkgonly_rebinned` | read by the gate |
        |---|---|---|---|
        | J100 unmasked | 0.0148562 | 0.0148783 | `_rebinned` |
        | J50 unmasked | 0.0024417 | 0.0024813 | `_rebinned` |
        | J50 masked | 0.0188064 | 0.0190617 | `_bkgonly_rebinned` |
        
        No recorded verdict changes — all three are unambiguous against the 0.01 threshold — so nothing
        published is affected. A fit landing between the two values would be accepted or rejected according
        to which histogram the gate happened to read, with no record of the choice. Left alone as a question
        for whoever owns the statistics, not a bug to be patched by picking one.
        
        **Fix.** Decide which histogram the goodness-of-fit gate is defined on, use it in both branches, and
        delete the comment. If the switch is deliberate — the masked fit's normalisation differs, which the
        comment above it hints at — say so there in a sentence instead.
        
        ### 40. Nothing checks fit status or covariance quality; every recorded fit has a forced covariance — **Medium** — **open; recorded, not fixed**
        
        **What.** `grep` for `covQual` or `status()` across `python/` and `scripts/` returns **nothing**: no
        part of the framework reads either. Every fit this repository has recorded was minimised with a
        covariance matrix MINUIT had to force positive-definite. From
        `run/run_481_3000_sixPar/quickFitLog_anaFit_sixPar_bkgOnly.log`:
        
        ```
        Warning in <Minuit2>: MnPosDef Matrix forced pos-def by adding to diagonal 0.00492847
                        covariance matrix quality: Full matrix, but forced positive-definite
                        Status : MINIMIZE=1 HESSE=1
        ```
        
        at every one of the retries, while the run's closing summary prints `Fit Summary of POIs (STATUS
        OK)`. All three recorded fits carry `status=1, covQual=2` in their baselines.
        
        **Where.** `python/` and `scripts/` generally — the absence is the issue. The values are visible in
        `FitResult_*.root`'s `fitResult` and in `quickFitLog_*.log`.
        
        **Affects.** The **parameter errors** rather than the central values. `covQual=2` means the matrix
        was full but forced positive-definite, so the fitted uncertainties come from a matrix with ~0.005
        added to its diagonal; the minimum itself is reported `Valid` and the retries land on the same FCN,
        which is what the 2026-09-15 14:38 CHANGELOG entry reasoned about. That entry is right about the
        minimum and silent about the errors, and the errors are what downstream studies — spurious signal,
        injection linearity, limits — consume. For J50/J100 the harness pins `status` and `covQual` exactly,
        so a *degradation* fails `check`; for any new configuration nothing checks, and `STATUS OK` is the
        last word the log prints.
        
        **Fix.** Read `fitResult.status()`/`covQual()` after the fit and print a clear line — ideally refuse
        to proceed below a configured `covQual`. Cheap, and it turns a property nobody sees into one
        decision. Whether `covQual=2` is acceptable for these fits is a physics judgement for the
        repository owner; this entry only records that the framework cannot currently tell you.
        
        ### 41. `getChi2` silently excludes bins with no data error or a non-positive fit — **Low** (latent) — **open; recorded, not fixed**
        
        **What.** The chi2 loop accumulates a bin only under `if valueErrorData > 0. and postFitValue > 0.`,
        and a skipped bin is counted in neither `chi2` nor `chi2bins`. An unweighted bin with zero observed
        events has zero error, so **empty bins are dropped from the goodness-of-fit and from the degrees of
        freedom**, with nothing reported. The exclusion is not numerically necessary: with
        `useSumW2=False` the residual is `(data - fit)/sqrt(fit)`, whose denominator is the *fit*, so a bin
        with zero data is perfectly computable. A dropped bin removes `fit` from the chi2 and 1 from ndof,
        so for a bin where the fit predicts more than about one event — an observation of zero against a
        prediction of several, i.e. a real deficit — the discarded term is the discrepant one.
        
        **Where.** [python/ExtractPostfitFromWS.py:59-76](python/ExtractPostfitFromWS.py#L59-L76).
        
        **Affects.** Nothing recorded. **Verified inactive in all three recorded fits**: every bin of every
        `PostFit_*.root` directory has a positive data error and a positive fit value, and the recorded
        `nbins` equals the histogram's own bin count in each case (J100 2519/57, J50 2695/65) — the only
        reduction anywhere is the masked J50 run dropping exactly its BumpHunter window (2695→2615 fine,
        65→62 rebinned), which is by design. It becomes reachable as soon as a fit range extends into the
        sparse high-mass tail where bins empty out, which is what a reach extension does. Left alone as
        latent.
        
        **Fix.** Guard on `postFitValue > 0` alone and let zero-data bins contribute, or keep the exclusion
        and report the count of skipped bins alongside `nbins` so it is visible in the chi2 block. The
        second is nearly free and does not change any recorded number.
        
        ### 42. `nPars` is a substring match on the background file's path, silently defaulting to 5 — **Low** — **open; recorded, not fixed**
        
        **What.** The number of background parameters is decided by testing the path for the words
        `three`…`ten`, and if none matches, `nPars` stays at its initialised value of **5**, with no
        message. `nPars` then sizes the prefit's parameter ranges, selects the PreFit function order and
        bounds the `PAR1..PARn` substitution loop. Two lines further on, the same function already parses
        the card's actual `[PAR<n>,` placeholders with a regex — so the information needed to check the
        guess is in hand and unused.
        
        **Where.** [python/run_anaFit.py:216-236](python/run_anaFit.py#L216-L236) (the derivation) against
        [python/run_anaFit.py:244-250](python/run_anaFit.py#L244-L250) (the card's real PAR indices).
        
        **Affects.** No card on the J50/J100 path: checked all twelve tracked `background_*.template` files,
        and every word-named one agrees with the highest `PAR<n>` its card declares (`fivePar`→5,
        `sixPar`→6, `sevenPar`→7, up to `tenPar`→10). Two real cases do disagree:
        `config/dijetTLAnlo/background_dijetTLAnlo_J100yStar06_CT14nnlo.template` gets `nPars=5` by default
        (benign — it declares no `PAR` placeholders at all), and a digit-named variant such as
        `…_6Par.template` would silently get 5.
        
        The collision hazard this first looked like is **smaller than it appears**, and that is worth
        recording so nobody re-raises it: the `elif` chain tests `four`, `five`, `six` before `seven`,
        `nine`, `ten`, so a spurious keyword elsewhere in the path cannot override the real one — checked
        with paths containing `stephen` and `tenPar_studies` around a `sixPar` card, both of which still
        give 6.
        
        What remains is the silent default. Too small, and a `PARn` placeholder is never substituted, so
        XMLReader fails — but warns and returns 0, and per issue 38 the process still exits 0. Too large,
        and PreFit fits a higher-order function and hands wrong starting values to a card of a different
        order, which produces a complete and plausible result from the wrong starting point.
        
        **Fix.** Compare against the card: `max` of the `PAR<n>` indices already parsed at line 244, and
        stop if it disagrees with `nPars`. Three lines, and it converts a naming slip from a silent wrong
        answer into a refusal.

Five findings, all on the **fit path** rather than the harness — so none was introduced by the reproducibility lock. Recorded as issues 38–42; no code touched.

**38 — `main()` discards the "failed fit" verdict. High.** This is the sharpest one. `run_anaFit()` computes the framework's only "this result is not acceptable" decision: p(chi2) fails, BumpHunter masks the most significant window, the fit is repeated, and if p(chi2) *still* fails it prints `Exiting with failed fit status.` and returns `-1`. That verdict is then thrown away twice — [run_anaFit.py:502](python/run_anaFit.py#L502) calls it with no `return`, so `sys.exit(None)` exits **0** (confirmed), and the driver doesn't check the exit code anyway, going straight on to render `postFit.pdf`, `post_fit.pdf` and the EDM plot. A twice-rejected fit is indistinguishable from an accepted one in every artefact except a line in the log. Fix is two words.

**39 — the p(chi2) gate reads a different histogram depending on whether a mask is active. Medium.** `<channel>_rebinned` unmasked, `<channel>_bkgonly_rebinned` masked, with the code's own `#should be <channel> or <channel>_rebinned?` comment showing it was never settled. From the baselines they differ by 1–2%: J50 masked is 0.0190617 via the gate's choice vs 0.0188064. **No recorded verdict changes** — all three fits are unambiguous against 0.01 — but a fit landing between the two would be accepted or rejected by which histogram got read.

**40 — nothing checks fit status or covariance quality. Medium.** `grep` for `covQual`/`status()` across `python/` and `scripts/` returns nothing, and every fit this repository has recorded ran at `covQual=2`: `Full matrix, but forced positive-definite`, `MINIMIZE=1 HESSE=1`, ~0.005 added to the diagonal at each retry — while the log's closing line reads `STATUS OK`. The 2026-09-15 CHANGELOG entry reasoned about this and is right about the *minimum*; it's silent about the *errors*, which is what a forced matrix degrades and what the downstream studies consume.

**41 — `getChi2` silently drops bins with no data error or non-positive fit. Low, latent.** Verified *not* triggered: every bin in both recorded runs has positive data and fit, and `nbins` equals the histogram bin count in all four directories. It bites when a range extends into the sparse tail. Worth noting the exclusion isn't numerically needed — the residual divides by `sqrt(fit)`, so zero-data bins are computable.

**42 — `nPars` is a substring match on the path, defaulting silently to 5. Low.** All twelve tracked cards agree with the `PAR<n>` they declare, so nothing is currently wrong. I also **disproved** the collision hazard it looks like: the `elif` chain tests `four`/`five`/`six` before `seven`/`nine`/`ten`, so a stray keyword in the path can't override the real one — recorded as a negative result so nobody re-raises it. What remains is the silent default, checkable for free against the PAR indices the code already parses two lines later.

Left alone per your standing rule that pre-existing fit-path bugs are recorded, not fixed — the rule that keeps issue 23 open. **38 is the one I'd ask you to decide on now:** the fix changes nothing about a passing run, but making the exit code meaningful could start surfacing genuine failures in anything that does check it (the HTCondor path), which is the point and worth doing deliberately. Want me to fix 38, or 38 plus 42's card cross-check?

        - [python/run_anaFit.py](python/run_anaFit.py): `main()` now does `return run_anaFit(…)` instead of
          calling it as a bare statement, so the `-1` returned by a fit that fails p(chi2) even with its
          BumpHunter window masked reaches `sys.exit` instead of being replaced by `None` (exit 0).

          prints an explicit `ERROR: run_anaFit.py exited N - … this result must not be used` banner, and
          reports the status as its own.

        Two decisions inside that fix, both deliberate:

        - **The plots are still produced on a failure.** They are the diagnostics you want in order to see
          *why* a fit failed, and suppressing them would trade one silent failure for another. What the fix
          removes is the run *reporting success*.
        - **`( exit … )`, not `exit`.** Both drivers are `{ … }` brace groups whose own headers say to
          source them (`. scripts/run_anaFit_run2.sh`), so a bare `exit` would kill an interactive shell;
          `tests/repro.py` meanwhile runs them with `bash`. A subshell exit sets `$?` correctly for both.
          `anafit_failed` is reset at the top of each run, because a sourced script would otherwise inherit
          a stale value from the previous one.

        `[PAR<n>,` matches into a l

    [tool] Write

        /tmp/hhook/claude-1062346/-afs-cern-ch-user-h-hhook-FrequentistFramework/d7a49d58-92fd-46b2-ae71-f3330fc9066b/scratchpad/improve.md
      content:

        ## The fit path's own verdict (`run_anaFit.py` and the Run 2 drivers)

        The framework computes one verdict on whether a fit is usable at all. If p(chi2) falls below
        `--maskthreshold` (default 0.01), `python/FindBHWindow.py` locates the most significant window, the
        fit is repeated with that window blinded, and if p(chi2) *still* fails, `run_anaFit()` prints
        `Exiting with failed fit status.` and returns `-1`.

        **That verdict is now reported.** It used to be discarded twice over — `main()` called
        `run_anaFit(…)` as a bare statement, so `sys.exit(None)` exited 0, and neither driver checked the
        exit code anyway — which meant a twice-rejected fit produced the same files, the same plots and the
        same successful exit as an accepted one ([KNOWN_ISSUES.md](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md) issue 38, fixed
        2026-09-17). Now:

        - `main()` returns `run_anaFit(…)`, so the status reaches `sys.exit`.
        - `scripts/run_anaFit_run2.sh` and `scripts/run_anaFit_run2_J50.sh` capture it, print an explicit
          `ERROR: … this result must not be used` banner, and report it as their own exit status.
        - **The plots are still produced on a failure**, deliberately: they are the diagnostics you want in
          order to see why the fit failed. What is no longer possible is the run reporting success.
        - The status is carried by a `( exit … )` subshell rather than `exit`, because both drivers are
          `{ … }` brace groups their own headers tell you to *source* — a bare `exit` would kill an
          interactive shell — while `tests/repro.py` runs them with `bash`.

        Anything that checks these drivers' exit status will therefore start seeing real failures it
        previously missed. That is the point of the change, but it is worth knowing before pointing the
        HTCondor path at it.

        **The parameter count is now cross-checked against the card.** `nPars` is derived by testing the
        background file's path for the words `three`…`ten`, falling back to 5 when none matches. The card
        itself is the authority — it declares `p1…pN` with `[PARn, …]` placeholders 
        [... 972 more characters truncated ...]
    -> result [file modified], 1 line(s)
       /tmp/hhook/claude-1062346/-afs-cern-ch-user-h-hhook-FrequentistFramework/d7a49d58-92fd-46b2-ae71-f3330fc9066b/scratchpad/improve.md

       # Improvements

       One living document for the whole reproducibility/refactoring effort: what the framework now
       does, why it was changed, and how it is meant to be used. Rewritten in place as things evolve —
       this describes the *current* state, not history. History is [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md).

       ## The fit path's own verdict (`run_anaFit.py` and the Run 2 drivers)

       The framework computes one verdict on whether a fit is usable at all. If p(chi2) falls below
       `--maskthreshold` (default 0.01), `python/FindBHWindow.py` locates the most significant window, the
       fit is repeated with that window blinded, and if p(chi2) *still* fails, `run_anaFit()` prints
       `Exiting with failed fit status.` and returns `-1`.

Both fixed and verified. Issues 38–42 are all recorded; 38 and 42 now marked **Fixed**, 39–41 left open with the reason.

**38 — fixed at the root and both live callers.** [run_anaFit.py:502](python/run_anaFit.py#L502) now does `return run_anaFit(…)`, so the `-1` reaches `sys.exit` instead of becoming `None`. Both Run 2 drivers capture the status, print an `ERROR: … this result must not be used` banner, and report it as their own. Two deliberate choices: the plots are **still** produced on a failure (they're the diagnostics you need to see why), and the status travels via `( exit … )` rather than `exit`, because both drivers are brace groups their own headers tell you to *source* — a bare `exit` would kill your shell — while `tests/repro.py` runs them with `bash`. Verified both ways.

**42 — fixed.** The card's `[PAR<n>,` matches are now gathered first, then the highest index is compared against the filename-derived `nPars` before the prefit and before the range assignment. All twelve tracked cards pass; the CT14nnlo card (no placeholders) warns; a `sixPar` card renamed `…_6Par` or `…_tenPar` is refused with both numbers.

**Verified:** `bash -n` clean on both drivers, `run_anaFit.py` parses, and a **full `check` — both analyses, real fits through the modified drivers, including J50's masking path — passed in 3m41s** with no baseline number moved and no `note: driver exited …`, which is the evidence the new success path still reports 0. Harness re-checked after the doc edits: `selfcheck`, `env` 26/26, `check --from` green on both run directories.

**One correction to my own analysis from last turn,** recorded in issue 42 rather than edited away: I said the too-small-`nPars` direction left a `PARn` placeholder unsubstituted so XMLReader "warns and returns 0". Wrong — `parRangeLow` is sized `nPars`, so a card with a higher index raised `IndexError` on the range assignment before any substitution. That direction failed closed all along; only `nPars` *larger* than the card declares was silent. The fix covers both and makes the first readable.
